Command: Do not eat animals that do not chew the cud or lack split hooves
Summary: A land animal is clean only if it both chews the cud and divides the hoof; an animal lacking either sign is unclean and may not be eaten.
Commandment: Do not eat any land animal that does not both chew the cud and divide the hoof.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The two-sign test gave Israel a plain rule for the herds and wild animals. The New Testament records these food distinctions set aside (Mark 7:19; Acts 10).
Purpose: To mark Israel's table as distinct (Leviticus 11). The New Testament records the distinctions set aside: Jesus declares all foods clean (Mark 7:19) and Peter's vision confirms it (Acts 10).
